pr_title: service: pass exiting service state to triggered On{Failure,Success}= dependencies
pr_body:
This PR adds support for passing exit status and other metadata to dependencies triggered via OnFailure= and OnSuccess=. The following environment variables are passed to the ```OnFailure=``` service ```ExecStart=``` and ```ExecStartPre=``` processes:

   * $MONITOR_SERVICE_RESULT
   * $MONITOR_EXIT_CODE
   * $MONITOR_EXIT_STATUS
   * $MONITOR_INVOCATION_ID
   * $MONITOR_UNIT

The first 3 variables are the same as those passed to ExecStop= and ExecStopPost= processes, however the values are related to the service which triggered the OnFailure=/OnSuccess= dependency.

The last 2 variables are new and as their names suggested are used to pass the invocation ID and unit name of the exiting service to the OnFailure= or OnSuccess= dependency.

This is useful for building more complex failure monitoring services.

Fixes #19885

issue_context.title: RFE: Add OnWatchdogFailure= dependency type
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'd like to be able to start some other service if systemd detects a service has not sent it's "WATCHDOG=1" message to systemd. This other service could be used to notify some other part of the system that a particular service wasn't able to pat the watchdog for whatever reason.

If a service has an OnFailure= dependency list and a OnWatchdogFailure= list then the OnWatchdogFailure dependencies would be run only if there was a watchdog failure. In all other failure cases the regular OnFailure dependency list would be run.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A new OnWatchdogFailure= dependency type which causes services specified to be run if the service which defines the list fails due to watchdog expiry.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I wondered about making use of the existing OnFailure= mechanism and then checking the services Result property for value "watchdog". This might be possible with templates and some other hoop jumping, thus the RFE for a clear mechanism for starting some service(s) on watchdog expiry.

**The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for**

249.
comments: So, we could add a concept that for OnFailure= and OnSuccess= we expose the service metainfo as env vars to the activated services. i.e. whenever we spawn a service we check the reverse deps OnFailureOf= and OnSuccessOf= it might have. If there's exactly one then we'd pick up up relevant props of the listed service and expose it as env vars in our service i.e. we'd basically take the env vars $EXIT_CODE=/$EXIT_STATUS=/$SERVICE_RESULT= that we currently set for ExecStop= of a service, and also set them for  any monitor service, maybe prefixed with MONITOR_ or so. Maybe also add MONITOR_UNIT= and MONITOR_INVOCATION_ID= as additional env vars describing the service OnFailureOf= and OnSuccessOf= point to.

Not a fan of OnWatchdogFailure=, it's a bit too specific to my test. I don't think we should permit an inflation of deps like this for every single case of failure tere might be. However, the simple approach i suggested should be equally good, no?
Yep, agreed. I like the more general approach here.

Quite frankly, i'd dumb this down. I mean, yes a failure unit could be started by multiple units, and that's fine, but I think we simply should not pass the metdata in that case where it is not unique.

instead: if there is anything not unique, let's just not pass metadata, let's only pass it if a unit got started as OnFailure=/OnSuccess= of exactly one other unit.

The failure unit being started by multiple units is a hard requirement for a reactive monitoring system, we can't lose data.

It can be consumed by scripts, see the unit test:

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/test/units/testsuite-68.sh#L79

> The failure unit being started by multiple units is a hard requirement for a reactive monitoring system, we can't lose data.

I don't follow? why is it a hard requirement to have a single unit that is triggered for a number of other units? why not just instantiate a small unit for each failing service? I mean, we have template units for a reason. i.e. `OnFailure=myfailurehandler@%n.service` is kinda how this is supposed to be used.
It needs to work for instances too - wasn't the infinite recursion issue fixed last year by making sure it can't happen in these cases? IE, the specifier doesn't get expanded past the first level

Well, yes and no. Should it work on instance units? yes, of course. Should it work recursively without limit? i.e. should you be able to have a monitor service for a monitor service for a monitor service. Nope. Certainly not.

My assumption is this: if you have a service called foo.service, then you'd do OnFailure=myfailurehandler@%p.service, but if you have quux@.service then you probably should do OnFailure=myfailurehandler@%p-%i.service or so. i.e. it's OK to tweak the instance to use.

I really don#t think it's a worthy goal to have a single service be executed for failures of a multitude of other services, because these other services will likely fail one by one, and not all atomically at the same moment. But only if they all share the exact same OnFailure= service then you'll likely get that service started exactly once, and it will process the first failure, but the rest will be ignored, because then the failure service is already running, and doesn't get started again. If you however use instances, then the problem goes away: each failing service will get its own failure service instance spawned which can process what is needed and then exit when its done: events will not be lost.
